LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 SELF-EXPRESSION – INTERVIEWS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we listen to get information from an aural text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify gender roles from aural texts for information
2. respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension
3. recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 SELF-EXPRESSION – INTERVIEWS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 SELF-EXPRESSION – INTERVIEWS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify gender roles from aural texts for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify gender roles from aural texts for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify gender roles from aural texts for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify gender roles from aural texts for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify gender roles from aural texts for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews to a partner. (skill: respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify gender roles from aural texts for information.
3. Practise this skill: respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: recognise the importance of listening purposefully for comprehension.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we listen to get information from an aural text?
2. Why should some opportunities be equal among both girls and boys?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify gender roles from aural texts for information.
5. Be able to: respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
